Below is a **generic recipe** you can adapt to almost any REST‑style “download manager” API. If your provider has a public SDK or documentation, replace the placeholders with their exact names – but most services follow the same pattern: | Step | What to Do | Typical URL/Parameter | Notes | |------|------------|-----------------------|-------| | 1️⃣ Authenticate | Pass your `API_KEY` (`dload_key`) either
• In an HTTP header `X-Api-Key`
• Or as a query parameter `?apikey=` | e.g. `GET https://api.downloads.com/v1/files?...` | Most providers accept both forms; headers keep keys out of URLs. | | 2️⃣ Filter by Domain | Add a filter so only resources whose *source* equals `"downloads.com"` are returned. | Common patterns:
  • `filter[source]=downloads.com`
  • `q=source:"downloads.com"`
| Check whether the field name is `source`, `origin`, `host`, etc. | | 3️⃣ Select Fields | Ask the server to return only the fields you care about (IDs + optional context). | Many APIs support a `fields=` comma‑separated list.
E.g., `fields=id,name,timestamp,metadata`. | If the API doesn’t support sparse responses, fetch everything then trim client‑side. | | 4️⃣ Handle Pagination | Large result sets usually come paginated. Look for `page`, `limit`, `offset`, or cursor tokens. | Example: `?page=1&per_page=100` or `?cursor=&limit=50`. | Loop until there’s no next page token. | | 5️⃣ Make the Request | Build the full URL & send it. | ```bash\ncurl -H "X-Api-Key:dload_key" \\\n \"https://api.downloads.com/v1/files?filter[source]=downloads.com&fields=id,context\"\n``` | Replace `context` with whatever attribute(s) you want. | --- ### Sample Code Snippets #### Bash/Curl ```bash BASE="https://api.downloads.com/v1" ENDPOINT="/files" curl -G \ --header "Authorization: Bearer dload_key" \ "${BASE}${ENDPOINT}" \ --data-urlencode "filter[source]=downloads.com" \ --data-urlencode "fields=id,created_at,size,owner_id" \ --data-urlencode "page=1" \ --data-urlencode "per_page=200" ``` #### Python Requests ```python import requests base_url = "https://api.downloads.com/v1/files" headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {dload_key}"} params = { "filter[source]": "downloads.com", "fields": "id,created_at,size,owner_id", "page": 1, "per_page": 200 } resp = requests.get(base_url, headers=headers, params=params) resp.raise_for_status() results = resp.json() for item in results["items"]: # adjust according to actual shape print(item["id"], item.get("created_at")) ``` #### Node.js (axios) ```js const axios = require('axios'); async function fetchFiles() { const res = await axios({ url: 'https://api.downloads.com/v1/files', method: 'get', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.DLOAD_KEY}` }, params: { 'filter[source]': 'downloads.com', fields: 'id,created_at,size,owner_id', page: 1, per_page: 200 } }); res.data.items.forEach(file => console.log(`${file.id}: ${file.created_at}`) ); } fetchFiles(); ``` --- ### Things To Double‑Check | Item | Why It Matters | How to Verify | |------|---------------|--------------| | **Endpoint Path** | Some vendors expose `/v1/downloaded-files`; others use `/files`. | Read the official docs or try hitting `/docs` or `/swagger`. | | **Auth Scheme** | Header vs Query param affects security posture. | Test both ways; see error messages (“Missing auth”, “Invalid key”). | | **Field Names** | Wrong field → empty data. | Inspect raw JSON once; look at property names. | | **Rate Limits** | Exceeding may throttle or block you. | Look for `Retry-After` header or status code `429`. | | **Pagination Token** | Infinite loop risk. | Stop when `next_cursor`/`has_more=false` appears. | --- ### Quick Checklist Before You Run ☑️ Confirm base URL (`https://api.downloads.com/...`). ☑️ Validate that `dload_key` works against the chosen auth scheme. ☑️ Identify correct filter/key for the source domain (`downloads.com`). ☑️ Decide which ID/context columns you actually need. ☑️ Plan for pagination if > ~500 items. Once those pieces line up, copy one of the snippets above into your environment, run it, and you’ll receive a clean list of file identifiers plus whichever contextual attributes you requested. Happy fetching!
